marketMood: Crosscurrents: IBM's shock 25% crash rattles tech/consulting while JPMorgan's blowout Q2 lifts financials — all against a backdrop of surging oil from the US–Iran Hormuz escalation and a surprise CPI monthly decline that hands the Fed a complex dilemma.

upcomingEvents.event: Fed Chair Warsh Senate Banking Committee testimony
China Q2 GDP + June Retail Sales & Industrial Output (NBS)

topStories.headline: IBM Stock Craters 25% After Shock Q2 Earnings Warning
topStories.summary: IBM released preliminary Q2 results showing revenue of $17.2B and EPS of $2.93, both missing estimates; CEO Arvind Krishna said clients diverted quarterly capex to servers, storage, and memory to secure supply-constrained hardware ahead of price increases, causing large consulting and software deals to miss close timelines.
topStories.marketImpact: IBM ↓ 25% — worst single-day decline on record. Panic spreading into software and IT-consulting peers; AI-as-a-service monetisation narrative challenged.

topStories.headline: June CPI Posts First Monthly Price Decline in Six Years; Annual Rate Cools to 3.5%
topStories.summary: US CPI fell 0.4% month-on-month in June — the first negative monthly reading since 2020 — pulling the year-on-year rate to 3.5% from May's 4.2%, driven mainly by lower energy costs; Fed Chair Warsh cautioned Congress that one good print is not 'mission accomplished' at 3.5% vs the 2% target.
topStories.marketImpact: Bonds ↑ (yields dipped); rate-cut hopes revived but Warsh's hawkish framing kept equity markets cautious; USD mixed.

topStories.headline: JPMorgan Posts Blowout Q2 Beat; Five Big Banks Report Strong Results
topStories.summary: JPMorgan reported Q2 EPS of $6.14 (vs $5.85 estimate) on revenue of $58.02B (vs $50.19B expected), driven by wealth management; Goldman, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, and Citigroup also reported Monday, broadly meeting or beating expectations.
topStories.marketImpact: JPM ↑; financials broadly bid ahead of Morgan Stanley's report today (July 15); lending and deal commentary will set tone for rest of earnings season.

topStories.headline: US–Iran Airstrikes Continue; Trump Abandons Hormuz Shipping Fee but Blockade Persists
topStories.summary: Trump abandoned his demand for a 20% cargo fee on Strait of Hormuz transits after announcing Gulf state trade and investment deals, but US airstrikes on Iran continued; only 6 ships crossed the Strait in a 12-hour window versus the usual 18–22, with roughly 230 loaded oil tankers stranded inside the Gulf.
topStories.marketImpact: WTI ↑ to $79.34/bbl (+1.5%), Brent ↑ to $84.73 (+1.7%); energy stocks XOM, CVX ↑; airlines and global industrials ↓; inflationary risk complicates Fed's path.

topStories.headline: Nikkei Slides 2%; Yaskawa Profit Warning and Oil Surge Compound Losses
topStories.summary: Japan's Nikkei 225 fell 1.98% to 67,197 on Monday as oil prices surged on Hormuz fears and Yaskawa Electric plunged 14.34% after Q1 net profit fell 21.7%; Murata Manufacturing shed 9.60% on component demand concerns.
topStories.marketImpact: 6506.T ↓ 14.3%; 6981.T ↓ 9.6%; Japanese manufacturers face rising energy import costs; Nikkei bank stocks MUFG (8306.T ↑ 2.3%) and SMFG (8316.T ↑ 1.6%) gained as investors rotated to value.

topStories.headline: SK Hynix Shares Continue Post-Nasdaq Rout After Record $26.5B Listing
topStories.summary: SK Hynix's Seoul-listed shares fell over 15% on Monday after its blockbuster Nasdaq ADR debut last week; the US-listed SKHY dropped a further 8% on Tuesday as investors continued to unwind positions following the largest-ever US listing by a foreign company.
topStories.marketImpact: SKHY ↓; Korean memory complex under pressure; analysts say structural AI memory demand remains intact but near-term sentiment is fragile.

topStories.headline: China Clears Shein for Hong Kong IPO; Listing Could Come as Early as September
topStories.summary: China's securities regulator (CSRC) approved Shein's Hong Kong Stock Exchange application; the IPO could raise low single-digit billions at an estimated $40–50B valuation — a steep discount from its $100B 2022 peak — after London and New York listing attempts were blocked by regulatory scrutiny over labour practices and transparency.
topStories.marketImpact: HK IPO pipeline ↑; HKEX sentiment ↑; Alibaba and Tencent (early Shein investors) watch; Western fast-fashion rivals (Inditex, H&M) potentially ↓.

topStories.headline: MiniMax Plans $2B Secondary Raise and Mainland China Listing
topStories.summary: Hong Kong-listed Chinese AI startup MiniMax — up 62.8% since its January 2026 HKEX IPO — announced plans to raise $2B via new shares and bonds and is pursuing a secondary listing on a mainland Chinese exchange, deepening its capital market presence.
topStories.marketImpact: Chinese AI sector sentiment ↑; HK fundraising momentum strengthens; Alibaba (9988.HK) and Tencent (0700.HK), both MiniMax backers, in focus.

companiesToWatch.name: IBM
companiesToWatch.reason: Shock Q2 earnings miss drove the stock to its worst single day on record (-25%); watch for contagion into Accenture, SAP, and Salesforce on concerns that enterprise AI consulting budgets are being cut.

companiesToWatch.name: JPMorgan Chase
companiesToWatch.reason: Blowout Q2 beat ($6.14 EPS vs $5.85 est.) set a high bar for today's Morgan Stanley report; management commentary on lending conditions and geopolitical risk will guide financial sector sentiment.

companiesToWatch.name: Morgan Stanley
companiesToWatch.reason: Reports Q2 earnings today (July 15, pre-market); consensus expects ~$2.89 EPS on $19.3B revenue, a ~36% year-on-year increase; wealth management and M&A advisory are the key metrics.

companiesToWatch.name: SK Hynix
companiesToWatch.reason: Continued selling following its record $26.5B Nasdaq debut; a stabilisation here would signal a floor for the AI memory supply chain and ease concerns about the Nasdaq listing's price discovery.

companiesToWatch.name: Yaskawa Electric
companiesToWatch.reason: Q1 net profit fell 21.7%, triggering a 14% share plunge; rising oil costs add further margin pressure for Japan's industrial robotics leader heading into the Tokyo session.

companiesToWatch.name: ExxonMobil
companiesToWatch.reason: Primary US beneficiary of the Hormuz disruption sending WTI above $79/bbl; watches for any ceasefire signal or further US–Iran escalation that could sharply reverse the oil rally.

quickHits: Fed Chair Warsh testifies to the Senate Banking Committee today (July 15) — yesterday's hawkish House testimony sent a clear signal that the Fed will not cut rates on a single month of soft CPI. (Bloomberg)
Murata Manufacturing (6981.T) fell 9.6% on Monday as rising oil prices raise input cost fears for Japanese electronic component makers, compounding sector-wide weakness. (Nikkei Asia)

China's AI companion content rules (CAC Interim Measures) took effect today — ByteDance's Doubao and Alibaba's Qwen are disabling custom persona features, resetting consumer AI monetisation timelines. (SCMP)

IBM's warning sent 'panic' into software and consulting stocks broadly, with Seeking Alpha flagging contagion risk across the enterprise IT sector after CEO Krishna admitted IBM 'faltered.' (Seeking Alpha)
